subject: Phased purge & recovery timeline proposal — Acme Health retention carveout
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-health.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: backup retention carveout + audit recovery window

Markus —

Thanks for taking this quickly. We’re onboarding Redwood for the next phase of our patient portal (go‑live Q3) and our internal compliance team flagged a couple of constraints for the upcoming audit. Short summary:

- Standard backup retention in our DPA is 30 days for snapshots and 90 days for logs.
- For the audit window (May 10–24) Acme Health needs an extended retention carveout for a small set of directories: patient intake forms and support transcripts. Specifically we need: 180 days snapshot retention for the named directories and a 14‑day emergency restore window that can be invoked by our security team (on demand) in case of requested evidence.
- We also need a clear list of subprocessors and the regions where backups are stored, and confirmation of key management (KMS) handling for any cross‑border copies.

Attached is our request memo with the list of affected object prefixes and the preliminary procurement ticket. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
  1) provide a retention carveout and an emergency restore workflow (on‑demand, 14‑day hold)
  2) provide a proposed phased purge timeline so we can plan our archive audit steps
  3) deliver an amendment to the DPA we can sign (DocuSign is preferred)

We’re on a tight timeline — the audit has a hard date and procurement wants an estimated cost for the carveout.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of IT Compliance, Acme Health
samir.patel@acme-health.com
Attachment: acme-data-retention-request.pdf

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Request: backup retention carveout + audit recovery window

Team — forwarding an urgent request from Acme Health (details attached). High level asks: 180‑day snapshot retention for a small set of prefixes + a 14‑day emergency restore window invoked by the customer during an audit. Procurement wants a cost estimate.

Proposed approach (draft):
1) Phased purge model:
   - Day 0–30: current hot snapshot retention (no change).
   - Day 31–180: move targeted prefixes to cold objects with cold storage tiering (readable, slower access). These objects remain recoverable for emergency holds.
   - Day 181+: permanent deletion unless customer has an active emergency hold or has converted the objects to long‑term archive under a paid carveout.
2) Emergency hold flow: customer raises a hold via portal + email to security@redwood.com; our on‑call ops runs a snapshot restore job that exports a time‑boxed archive to a secure, access‑restricted bucket for up to the requested hold period (default 14 days). Restore SLA target: 48–72 hours from hold activation for cold tier requests.
3) Subprocessor and KMS details: compile current list (will attach CSV) and call out any cross‑border replication. Confirm whether customer needs HSM/KMS exclusivity for keys (that affects procurement).
4) Pricing: chargeable line items for cold storage increase, restore job execution, and extended retention—provide both one‑time and monthly amortized options.

Kimberly — can you draft the DPA amendment/redline (include the phased purge language + emergency hold mechanics)? Laura — can you scope impact to Dedicated/Hosted tiers (which pools have the affected subproc storage) and confirm any quota or SLA implications? Rishi — please flag any operational constraints for a 48–72 hour restore SLA.

I’ll craft the external response once you have a draft. Keep it tight; Acme is time sensitive.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: backup retention carveout + audit recovery window

Markus / team — attaching a redline of the DPA amendment that captures: specific prefixes (we should insert the list from Acme’s PDF), phased purge timelines, emergency hold process, restore SLA, and the cost table. I left two TBDs: explicit HSM/KMS exclusivity and whether Acme requires subprocessor contractual flow‑downs (i.e., copies hosted by our cloud partner in eu‑west).

Notes on the draft:
- I used a 48–72 hour target for cold restores but added an exception for unusually large datasets (>2TB) where restore window may be extended and priced separately.
- Emergency hold activation language requires both a portal request and an authorized signatory (to prevent accidental holds).
- Added a cap: emergency hold will not exceed 14 days unless a longer period is explicitly requested and approved by legal (this matches their ask).

Attachments: dpa-amendment-draft-redline.docx, acme-cost-estimate.csv

Next steps: once legal signs off we can send to Acme with a proposed DocuSign packet. Laura — I called out which storage pools are affected in the comments of the cost spreadsheet.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
Attachments: dpa-amendment-draft-redline.docx; acme-cost-estimate.csv

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-health.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T14:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: backup retention carveout + audit recovery window — Proposed phased purge & emergency recovery

Samir — thanks for the clarity. Attached is our proposed plan (PDF) and the current subprocessors CSV. Summary below and a DocuSign link to the DPA amendment for signature: https://www.docusign.com/en/sign/ABC1234

Proposed timeline (targets):
- Immediate (within 7 days of signed amendment): enable retention flag for listed prefixes; snapshot lifecycle updated to retain 180 days for those prefixes.
- Day 0–30: objects remain in hot storage (no access latency change).
- Day 31–180: objects transitioned to cold tier (readable via restore job).
- Day 181+: automated deletion unless an active emergency hold exists or the customer opts into long‑term archive (separate pricing).

Emergency hold & restore process:
- Activation: authorized Acme security officer files a portal request + confirmation email to security@redwood.com.
- Execution: ops schedules a restore/export; target completion for cold tier restores is 48–72 hours; expedited restores (within 24 hours) available at premium rate.
- Hold duration: default 14 days (customer may request extension; extensions require approval and may incur fees).
- Access control: restored archives are placed into a restricted bucket with KMS encryption; access logs and audit trail are retained for 1 year.

Subprocessors / data transfer notes:
- Current subprocessors with backup access are listed in attached CSV (subprocessors-current-20270403.csv). Replication to eu‑west occurs only for disaster recovery for some Hosted pools; we’ve flagged those rows. All backups remain encrypted in transit and at rest; by default we manage keys in our KMS but can support customer‑managed keys under Private deployments (this requires a separate key agreement).

Costs: see attached estimate (acme‑cost‑estimate.csv) — two options provided (one‑time restore + monthly amortized storage).

If this plan looks acceptable I’ll send the DocuSign packet for the amendment and we’ll schedule the config change once signed.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
Attachments: proposed-purge-timeline.pdf; subprocessors-current-20270403.csv

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-health.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-health.com
Date: 2027-04-04T17:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: backup retention carveout + audit recovery window — Proposed phased purge & emergency recovery

Markus / Kimberly / Laura —

Thanks — the plan reads well and addresses most of our concerns. Two minor changes we need before sign‑off:
1) Increase the maximum emergency hold duration to 30 days (we will try to keep to 14 but need the option for 30 days in rare cases).
2) Please add the region column next to subprocessors with explicit whether backup replicas are stored in the US only or also in EU/APAC — our privacy team needs that text for the audit packet.

Also confirm encryption key handling: per our compliance policy, if Redwood manages KMS keys, we need a written confirmation that key rotation and access logs meet SOC 2 controls (we may request the KMS attestation). If you support customer‑managed keys under Private, include the integration note in the amendment.

Procurement reference: HS-99877 (they’ll use this to match the invoice). I’ve attached a signed intent PDF to speed the internal approvals.

If you can update the amendment with the two small changes I’ll route for signatures. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of IT Compliance, Acme Health
samir.patel@acme-health.com
Attachment: signed-exception-intent.pdf
